symptom: `mxcli describe -p app.mpr published rest service M.Api` prints `Unknown type: published rest service` (also for `publishedrestservice`), and `mxcli describe -p app.mpr M.Api` reports `no describable document named "M.Api"`, while the MDL statement `describe published rest service M.Api` works in `exec`, `-c` and the REPL
cause: The describe subcommand keeps its own hand-written type-to-statement switch and two auto-detect maps; published REST services were added to the grammar and executor but never to that switch, `objectTypeToDescribe` (catalog `PUBLISHED_REST_SERVICE`) or `unitTypeToDescribe` (`Rest$PublishedRestService`)
insight: The CLI dispatch is a second copy of the DESCRIBE grammar and drifts from it silently. Extracting the switch into a pure function made it testable; the guard that pays off is a test that every keyword auto-detect can emit is accepted by the dispatch, so a new map entry without a dispatch case fails. Comparing the switch with `describeStatement` in MDLCatalog.g4 lists the other forms still missing from the CLI (rule, javascript action, icon collection, message definition, contract entity/action/message, ...).
